mentl/20aa6fd:
Records work through every layer. `{name: "Morgan", age: 30}` parses,
infers, lowers, emits. Field access via `p.name` gains its missing
producer. Pattern destructure `{name, age}` binds locals.

Substrate decisions:
  - Structural records only (v1). No declaration syntax; the type IS
    the shape. `type Person = {...}` is deferred to H2.3 if it lands.
  - Untagged heap layout — fields at byte offset 4*i in name-sort
    order. Records carry identity in the type system; runtime sees
    raw fields. LMakeRecord mirrors LMakeVariant minus the tag word.
  - Field punning desugars at parse time. `{name}` becomes
    `{name: name}` before reaching infer; downstream sees uniform
    MakeRecordExpr.
  - PRecord patterns always-match. No tag check at runtime — the
    type system has already proven the scrutinee fits. Field binds
    use pre-resolved offsets baked at lower time.

Files:
  types.ka — MakeRecordExpr(List) added to Expr.
  parser.ka — parse_brace_expr disambiguates {} between record and
    block via 2-token lookahead (Ident Colon | Ident Comma|RBrace).
    parse_record_literal + parse_record_fields with field-puning
    desugar. parse_pat gains TLBrace arm for PRecord. parse_type_ty
    gains TLBrace arm for TRecord type literal. Insertion sort by
    name applied at every record-construction boundary.
  infer.ka — MakeRecordExpr inference (TRecord with TVar(value_h)
    field types). PRecord pattern inference: bind scrutinee to
    TRecordOpen(field_specs, fresh_row_var); recurse on sub-pats
    against per-field handles. unify_types gains TRecord/TRecordOpen
    arms with full closed×closed, closed×open, open×open algebra.
    Helpers: unify_record_fields_loop, find_record_field_pos,
    intersect/diff/subset over field lists.
  lower.ka — MakeRecordExpr → LMakeRecord (sorted-by-name values
    threaded through). LPRecord variant carries pre-resolved byte
    offsets per field. cfv_record_fields walks free-variable use
    in record-literal values.

mentl/20cf1f3:
Three bugs found and fixed in the self-hosted compiler:

1. codegen.lux emit_state_offsets: was emitting sequential indices (0,1,2...)
   instead of resolving state variable names to their actual offsets. Added
   ctx_state_names field (11th ctx element) and find_state_offset lookup.
   The old code had a literal TODO: "Full state name resolution would match
   update names to handler state names."

2. infer.lux map(resolve, param_types): passed an effect operation as a bare
   value. Effect operations aren't first-class — `resolve` alone resolves to
   Unit. Wrapped in lambda: map(|t| resolve(t), param_types). This was the
   root cause of "cannot call value: () in handler:yield" when checking 2+
   FnStmts from a script.

3. codegen.lux find_state_offset: returned 0 on not-found (silent corruption).
   Now returns -1 sentinel, matching find_local/find_name/find_upvalue.

Also: check.lux reverted from effect-based unification (subst_bind/subst_apply)
to pure function threading — the effect approach had re-entrant evidence dispatch
issues. effects.rs .unwrap_or(0) → panic on missing state name.

check_program now works when called from Lux scripts. Prelude checks clean
(190 entries). Bootstrap compiler compiles to WASM.

The out-of-band MatchOver write can no longer roll back. Forfeit, goodbye
and desync all end a match from outside GgrsSchedule, which CONVENTIONS
forbids for a reason: on the goodbye path the session is still alive
with the peer's trailing inputs in flight, and the next rollback restored

disconnect timeout ended it again. The audit's proposed fix (route it
through sim::apply_rematch "like the rematch flag") does not exist:

noodles/20dd5b5:
The stated ideal flow is build/perform in session view, arm record and
perform scene changes and mutes, then tidy in the arrangement and
export. Scene changes were captured; mute moves were not — a
filter-the-drums-out-then-slam-them-back drop shaped the take you heard
and then vanished from the recording, because the mixer is live-only
state.

Now the take keeps the drop. Session record writes each track's
effective audibility (mute OR un-soloed) into a bar-quantized lane,
song.mutes[track][bar], alongside the scene capture — re-recording a
section overwrites it, undo covers it (it lives in the song), and old
projects load with empty lanes. Playback gates note scheduling per bar
in playArrangementStepOn, the single path shared by the live
arrangement, master, stems, and loop exports, so the mute performance
replays everywhere. Tails ring out across the boundary on purpose: it
is a bar-quantized stop, not a hard channel gate. Faders and sends stay
static per project — mutes are the groovebox move, not DAW automation.

The arrangement shades recorded mutes as hatched runs painted over the
clips, so the silence is visible where you trim; the ? guide's record
line now tells the whole story.

Verified end to end: real M-button toggles during an armed take land as
drums=00001100 (bar-quantized, other lanes untouched); a [0,0,1,1] lane
renders the drums stem at -9.6/-9.6/-55/-180 dB per bar (clean kit —
first muted bar is the natural tail, second is digital silence);
overlays land at exact bar positions; smoke passes.

bits/206b70e:
The audit's blockers, plus the one change that decides whether a person
can start a bit at all.

Sound no longer has to come from the mic. "use a file" sits beside
"record the bit" on the first screen and takes a voice memo, a song, or
the audio off a video; an audio-only container is kept byte for byte, a
video is decoded to its audio and re-encoded rather than stored whole,
and a file with no audio track says so plainly. Asking someone to talk
out loud before anything happens was the widest part of the funnel.

Nothing is lost by accident. Deleting a bit opens a menu, not a bare
cross inside the row's own tap area; it moves the recipe to trash/ and
offers five seconds of undo, and the assets are only collected when that
window closes. A window interrupted by a closing tab is swept on the next
launch, so an abandoned delete can neither lose a bit nor leak storage.
Holding a puppet no longer deletes it. Dropping one from the tools is
undoable. A recipe that will not parse is no longer swapped silently for
a blank project: the bytes are kept and offered back as a file.

No dead ends. An error is a dismissible banner over a stage that stays
mounted, instead of one line of text replacing the whole screen. An empty
stage says to cast a puppet and gives you two ways to do it. Play works
as soon as there is sound, so mouths and wires can be previewed before
any pass exists. Casting a photo shows progress across the model download
and says when it kept the whole frame. The foley strip moved below the
stage, where five pills fit without clipping or covering the puppets you
are reaching for.

No system dialogs anywhere: prompt and confirm became in-app sheets.
MediaPipe is now imported dynamically, which took the initial payload
from 237.5KB to 197KB gzipped and honours "the models stay lazy".
